body.brief: Read a cross section of the corpus, open the lanes to add to as the main projects run, and add to them.

body.subtask: cross-check the three ports' canonical form against ONE shared vector set, and find who was wrong
body.why: the fleet has three ports of one chain rule and each was tested only against its own golden

body.prompt: Do the three ports agree, everywhere, or only on the samples?
body.response: Not everywhere. The rule has THREE exponent bands: Rust (ryu, normative) uses the exponent form iff kk<=-5 or kk>=17; Python (repr) iff kk<=-4 or kk>=17; Go (strconv 'g') iff kk<=-4 or kk>=7. Python was wrong on 11 of 40, Go on 18 of 40. The shared vector file had been generated BY THE PYTHON, so it recorded the Python's spelling as normative and was wrong on 2 of its own 21 cases -- and the Rust failed it on the first run while the Python that wrote it passed.

body.subtask: regenerate the vectors FROM the normative port, then fix the ports that disagree -- never the vectors
body.why: a shared vector file only fixes the divergence if the vectors come from the port the spec names

measurements: 3 exponent bands: Rust kk<=-5 or kk>=17, Python kk<=-4 or kk>=17, Go kk<=-4 or kk>=7
Python wrong on 11 of 40 boundary cases; Go wrong on 18 of 40
the shared vectors were generated by the Python and were wrong on 2 of their own 21 cases
the old vector set had nothing in [1e-5,1e-4) -- exactly where the Python was wrong; 21 -> 40, both sides of every boundary
118,320 values (1,184 subnormals, 55,382 >= 1e16) against serde_json: 0 mismatches in both shipped formatters
break each port's rule and its own test goes red: Go 18 cases, Python 11, the reference 15
receipt.note: every number in both pieces is a measurement, and the measurement is re-derivable
receipt.witness: this chain re-derives; verify with python3 labs/situation-recorder/recorder.py --verify sit-2026-10-19-golden-and-vectors.jsonl
